title: MARINE AND COASTAL POLLUTION - EXPRO+
description: In the framework of the Earth Observation Applications projects, the Marine and Coastal Pollution project aims to develop innovative high-quality EO-based information products, indicators and methods to improve the monitoring and attribution of marine and coastalpollution. This activity is linked to a number of key policies at international (e.g. UNFCCC, UN SDGs, 2022 Kunming-Montreal GlobalBiodiversity Framework (GBF), Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement, the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL).) and European (e.g., the European Ocean Pact, the ZeroPollution Action Plan, the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, the Water Framework Directive (WFD)) levels.The activity targets bothland-based pollution (e.g. urban runoff, agricultural fertilizers, industrial waste) of the coastal environment and marine-basedpollution (e.g. shipping, offshore infrastructure, aquaculture, dredging) in the coastal and open ocean. A detection-attribution modelling framework shall be developed integrating EO data with relevant ancillary information (e.g. with vessel/AIS data, offshore infrastructure and activity information, metocean conditions, ocean circulation models and other relevant datasets) to identify and analyse the sources, drivers and transport pathways of pollution and their contribution to observed patterns of water quality and environmental variability in coastal and open-ocean waters.Such framework shall enable:-the monitoring and modelling of key indicators of marine and coastal environmental quality and pollution, including eutrophication, surface water temperature anomalies, changesin turbidity, harmful algal blooms, oil and hydrocarbon pollution, floating marine litter and other pollution indicators affecting the marine and coastal ocean health;-the establishment of linkages between observed environmental and water quality patterns and pollution sources, including terrestrial and marine-based activities, as well as the identification of associated transport pathways,likely sources and areas of recurrent pollution.The project shall have a multi-sensor approach, leverage on state-of-the-art existing datasets and integrate as necessary open non-EO data, in-situ measurements and model outputs. This activity is considered in the series of the PEOPLE (Pioneering EO apPLications for the Environment) projects and it shall be implemented in close collaboration with early adopters: government agencies, environmental organisations and private companies from the Blue Economy sector.  The EA shall beinvolved in the requirements consolidation and the validation process of the new methods and relative derived information products.This activity requires an open-science approach, sharing knowledge and information across the stakeholders and end-users.

title: NAVISP-EL1-133-RESILIENT PNT BY A COMBINED GNSS/ELORAN/INS APPROACH FOR U-SPACE APPLICATIONS EXPRO+
description: This activity will define a hybrid Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) concept for U-space Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS)drone operations under EU Regulation 2021/664. GNSS-only solutions are vulnerable to jamming and spoofing, and their performance islimited by multipath propagation and long PPP convergence times. The proposed concept is a loosely coupled PNT stack combining Galileo OSNMA authentication, Galileo HAS high-accuracy corrections, eLoran timing, a barometric altimeter and inertial sensors. It buildson previous NAVISP work on compact H-field eLoran antennas and integrated GNSS/eLoran receivers. The activity will assess how timing aiding can accelerate PPP convergence, improve resilience to interference and spoofing, support GNSS fault detection, and provide PNT-health indicators for U-space services such as Remote ID, Flight Authorisation and Geo-awareness. It will propose KPIs, reference datasets and test methods for assessing hybrid PNT performance, and consider how hybrid-PNT integrity information could support SORA safety assessments and Remote ID position reporting. The outputs will include a reference architecture for timing-aided hybrid PNT, a conceptual UAV-based demonstrator outlining a pathway towards TRL 4, and recommendations for future higher-TRL developments.

This tender addresses the next phase of the EVDC's evolution: EVDC Nova. This initiative will establish the foundations for a robust, operational multi-mission platform while ensuring the complete continuity of existing services

title: AI/ML APPLICATION TO ENHANCE SPACE WEATHER FORECASTING CAPABILITY WITH THE VIGIL MISSION - EXPRO PLUS
description: This activity aims to investigate and develop advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) methodologies for solar flare and CME prediction. The objective is to improve both the accuracy and latency of forecasting systems by exploiting large, multi-source observational datasets and modern data-driven techniques. Particular emphasis will be placed on the prediction of CME characteristics relevant to downstream space weather impacts, including propagation speed, density, trajectory, and magnetic field properties.

title: END-TO-END DEMONSTRATOR RADAR FOR SPACE OBJECT DETECTION - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop and validate an end-to-end demonstrator of a multistatic radar system for space object detection and tracking using cooperative and non-cooperative signals from diverse satellites. The activity evaluates the integration within NewSpace LEO constellations to support advanced surveillance, monitoring, and situational awareness services.Description:  The activity focuses on the development and validation of a complete end-to-end testbed demonstrator for multistatic radar object detection. The system shall operate by receiving and processing reflected signals from multiple satellites, regardless of whether they are designed forcooperative use (e.g. hosted beacons or known signal providers) or non cooperative (e.g. opportunistic use of signals transmitted for other purposes). The aim is to build a prototype capable of operating in representative environments, addressing the practical implementation of hardware and software elements, as well as system integration within NewSpace LEO constellations.  The system designed in this activity focuses on detecting, localizing, and tracking space objects through the reception and processing of reflected signals. Theactivity targets to validate detection performance in controlled settings, assess spatial coverage and scalability, and propose strategies for real-world deployment. A key objective is to enable seamless integration into existing or planned LEO constellations viaflexible architectures, such as hosted payloads or onboard processing modules. The use of a multilayer sensing approach will also be evaluated. The results of this activity aims to contribute to space capabilities in Space Situational Awareness (SSA) and Space Traffic Management (STM), Resilience and Security of Space Assets. The system developed in this activity shall be designed to detectand correlate both direct and reflected signals, supported by the development of advanced algorithms for object detection, tracking,and clutter suppression. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Provide a comprehensive state-of-the-artand feasibility baseline to drive the design of the radar demonstrator architecture. - - - - Provide a complete end-to-end systemarchitecture specification and a technical reference model for demonstrator implementation. Develop a modular, end-to-end software simulator thatmodels the transmission processing chain, signal-object interaction, and receiver-side processing. Develop the functional breadboardimplementations of both the transmitter and receiver chains. Execute a controlled environment validation of thebreadboards and provide experimental validation results. Deliverables: Breadboard, Prototype, ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTPWork Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating stateswill be known at tender issue.
